constraint_decided_it: AP21 contains (A2 -> E18) is declared in CRMarchaeo as 'a shortcut for the more detailed path from E18 Physical Thing through AP18i is embedded, A7 Embedding, AP19 is embedding in, A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit'. That declaration is the whole answer to the question asked ('may we link the find straight to the context?'): the flat link is legal but is a shortcut, and only its expansion can be qualified. B surfaces AP21 and rejects it on exactly that ground; A never mentions it and instead asserts 'CRM gives no other class' for a direct link, which is false as stated. Second discriminator: A7's scope note bounds an embedding to have been stable 'from the time of generation of the first instance of A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit that surrounds it', its only exception being 'later intrusion' -- i.e. the embedding may be younger than the deposit, never older. Residuality is the opposite direction, so the A7 layer cannot carry it. B still routes residuality correctly, through the axe's own E12 Production (Neolithic) held separate from the deposit's stratigraphic genesis; A explicitly loads it onto the A7 Embedding ('use that layer to carry the excavators' note that this embedding is not contemporary with the deposit's formation'), where the scope note will not hold it.

What neither fully reached: residuality is not a property of the embedding at all. Record it as a time-span mismatch between two separate events -- the axe's E12 Production (Neolithic) and the deposit's A4 Stratigraphic Genesis (post-Roman) -- and, since Issue 447 (closed Done, 'A7 Embedding and its properties were updated to reflect its feature-like nature') makes A7 a feature with its own genesis event, date the A7 Embedding itself to the colluviation, which is contemporary with the A2's genesis and not with the axe. The find event is S19 Encounter Event within the A9 Archaeological Excavation; S19's scope note supplies the in-situ vocabulary. AP21 may be retained as the shortcut the database already records, expanded to the A7 path where qualification is needed.
